findings.title: Malformed Retry-After header raises ValueError out of the retry path
findings.description: On Python 3.10+ `email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime` raises `ValueError` for an unparseable date instead of returning `None`. Reaching line 128 means `float(raw)` already failed, so any non-numeric, non-HTTP-date `Retry-After` (e.g. a proxy sending `Retry-After: soon`) on a 429/503 propagates a bare `ValueError` out of `request()` instead of retrying or raising a `DialgemError` subclass.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the parse in `try/except (TypeError, ValueError)` and fall through to `None` so the caller uses `_backoff(attempt)`.

findings.title: Restore step rewrites CRLF source files as LF
findings.description: `read_text` uses universal newlines, so `original` holds `\n` even for a CRLF working file; writing it back with `newline=""` performs no translation, so every mutated file ends up LF after the "restore". On a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` the tree is left dirty even when the script succeeds.
findings.suggestion: Read and write bytes instead (`path.read_bytes()` / `path.write_bytes()`), decoding only for the `count`/`replace` step, so the restore is byte-faithful.

findings.title: Inline subscribe/getSnapshot re-subscribe the media query on every render
findings.description: `useSyncExternalStore` re-runs unsubscribe + subscribe whenever the `subscribe` function changes identity. Both callbacks here are created inline inside `useIsDesktop`, so each render of `GemPanel` tears down the `change` listener, builds a fresh `MediaQueryList`, and attaches a new one. The listener is correctly removed so nothing leaks, but the churn is pure waste on a component that re-renders with every `useGem()` state change.
findings.suggestion: Consider hoisting the query and the three callbacks to module scope (a single shared `MediaQueryList` plus stable `subscribe`/`getSnapshot`/`getServerSnapshot` constants) so the identities are stable across renders.

findings.title: Unthrottled capture-phase scroll handler does a forced layout per event
findings.description: While the menu is open, every scroll event anywhere in the page (capture: true catches inner scrollers too) runs `measure()`, which inserts a mirror div into `document.body`, reads `getComputedStyle` plus `getBoundingClientRect`, and then calls `setPlace` with a fresh object — a forced synchronous layout and a React re-render per scroll tick, which fires dozens of times per second during a trackpad/wheel scroll of the agent editor.
findings.suggestion: Consider coalescing the handler into one `requestAnimationFrame` (drop events while a frame is pending), and bailing out of `setPlace` when the computed placement is unchanged.

findings.title: A fractional GEM_USER_DAILY_CREDITS silently means "no limit"
findings.description: Credits are half-granular everywhere else (`WEIGHTS` has 0.5, the PUT body takes a float and rounds to halves, the UI validates halves), but this env parse uses `int(raw)`, so `GEM_USER_DAILY_CREDITS=2.5` raises ValueError and falls through to `0` — which this module documents as "no limit". An operator setting a fractional per-person cap gets the opposite of what they asked for, with nothing logged.
findings.suggestion: Consider parsing with `float`/`Decimal` so halves are honoured (and keeping 0 only for an unset or genuinely unparseable value).

findings.title: Export carries built-in function credentials in `config`
findings.description: `_FUNCTION_FIELDS` includes `config`, and for built-in function kinds that JSON holds live credentials — `app/agent/functions_builtin.py:301-311,426` reads `config["cal_api_key"]` and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer`. An agent with a Cal.com booking function exported via `GET /v1/agents/{id}/export` therefore writes that API key verbatim into a file the dashboard downloads to disk and users share/import elsewhere, even though `headers` was deliberately excluded for exactly this reason and the module docstring promises no credentials. The existing round-trip test only asserts `webhook_signing_secret` is absent, so this passes unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Strip credential keys out of each function's `config` in `build_export` (at minimum `cal_api_key`, and consider `integration_id`, which points at one org's stored OAuth tokens), and drop the same keys in `parse_import` so an imported document cannot carry someone else's key in.

fix.oldText: fns.append({k: copy.deepcopy(f[k]) for k in _FUNCTION_FIELDS if k in f})

findings.title: Assistant preamble text is emitted after the tool lines it preceded
findings.description: In the block-content branch the `tool_use`/`tool_result` lines are appended inside the loop while the message's own `text` blocks are only appended afterwards (line 929). For an Anthropic assistant turn shaped `[{text: "One moment."}, {tool_use ...}]` (exactly what `_append_tool_exchange` writes when `text_parts` is non-empty), the flattened history reads "[called book(...)]" and only then "One moment.", inverting what the agent actually said relative to the call.
findings.suggestion: Collect the text blocks and `_add` them before walking the tool blocks, so the preamble keeps its position ahead of the call it introduced.

findings.title: Strategy 3 clears an edge_id strategy 1 already resolved
findings.description: Strategy 1 can set `edge_id` while leaving `node_id` None — that happens exactly when the node dict was found by index but carries no usable `id` (e.g. `{"edges": [{"id": "e1", ...}]}` with a missing/blank node id, which is itself a reportable error). The new tuple assignment then unconditionally overwrites `edge_id` with `_owner_by_value`'s `None`, so the edge locator that was already recovered is lost.
findings.suggestion: Consider only adopting the strategy-3 result when it actually resolved a node, leaving a previously-found `edge_id` intact otherwise.

fix.oldText:
if node_id is None:
        node_id, edge_id = _owner_by_value(body, path, input_value)

findings.title: Org combobox queries on every keystroke
findings.description: The query key is the path containing the raw `text`, so each keystroke in the picker issues a fresh GET /v1/admin/orgs. That endpoint (services/agent/app/routers/admin_data.py:93) runs a COUNT plus seven correlated subqueries per returned row, so typing a slug fires ~8 of those in a second, concurrently with the list's own filtered query.
findings.suggestion: Consider feeding a debounced copy of `text` (~200ms) into the request path, so only the settled term hits /v1/admin/orgs.

findings.title: Per-tab impersonation flag guards a browser-wide session cookie
findings.description: The read-only guarantee relies on `dialgem_impersonating` in sessionStorage (per tab), but `setSessionToken` writes the view-as JWT to `document.cookie` (`dialgem_session`, path=/, 30-day max-age), which is shared by every tab in the browser. If the staff member also has their own dashboard open, that tab is not flagged: its pre-expiry timer / 401 path calls `refreshSession()`, which trades the staff refresh cookie and overwrites the shared cookie with a staff token — silently ending the view-as session mid-use — and until then the staff tab is issuing requests with the customer's `imp` token (the auth-provider's `apiSwitchOrg` re-scope is also unguarded there). Writes are still blocked by the server's `imp` claim, so this is cross-session interference rather than privilege escalation, but the documented "never refreshed, never logged out" property only holds when exactly one dialgem tab exists.
findings.suggestion: Consider carrying the view-as token in a distinct, impersonation-only cookie name (or keying `dialgem_session` per tab) so a normal tab cannot refresh over it, or derive `isImpersonating()` from the token's `imp` claim via `readTokenClaims(getSessionToken())` instead of per-tab sessionStorage, so every tab reaches the same conclusion.

findings.title: sign-out of a staff account is not restricted to superadmin
findings.description: `sign_user_out` is gated on `users.manage` (admin + support) and only resolves the user by id — it has no staff-account guard. `POST /v1/admin/users/<superadmin-user-id>/sign-out` from a support-tier token revokes that superadmin's entire refresh family. The sibling endpoint built for exactly this, `revoke_staff_sessions` in admin_staff.py, requires `staff.manage` (superadmin only), and `disable_user` in this same file refuses a target with a non-NULL `platform_role` — so the privilege boundary is drawn everywhere except here.
findings.suggestion: Consider refusing a target with a non-NULL `platform_role` here, as `disable_user` does, and routing staff sign-out through the `staff.manage`-gated endpoint.

fix.oldText:
user = await _user_or_404(db, user_id)
    n = await revoke_all_sessions(db, user.id)
fix.newText:
user = await _user_or_404(db, user_id)
    if user.platform_role is not None:
        raise _err(409, "STAFF_ACCOUNT", "Use the staff session controls for a staff account.")
    n = await revoke_all_sessions(db, user.id)

findings.title: session ip / user_agent are the lexicographic max, not the latest
findings.description: `func.max(RefreshToken.ip)` and `func.max(RefreshToken.user_agent)` are aggregated independently of `func.max(created_at)`, so a family that rotated across addresses reports the alphabetically-largest string (e.g. `9.9.9.9` over a later `10.0.0.5`) rather than the one from the most recent token — and the ip and user_agent shown can even come from different rows. Staff read these fields to judge whether a session looks suspicious.
findings.suggestion: Consider taking ip/user_agent from the latest row of each family — e.g. a `DISTINCT ON (family_id) ... ORDER BY family_id, created_at DESC` subquery, or `row_number()` — instead of aggregating them.

findings.title: Failed dry-run leaves the cleanup dialog stuck on "Checking…"
findings.description: The dry-run is fired and `cleanup.current?.showModal()` opens the dialog in the top layer; the only error surface (`{err && …}` above `AdminList`) sits under the modal backdrop and is unreachable. If `POST /v1/admin/orgs/purge` fails (403, 5xx, network), `preview` stays null, so the dialog shows "Checking…" forever with no way to see why and no retry.
findings.suggestion: Render the purge error inside the dialog next to the "Checking…" placeholder (and ideally offer a retry), so a failed dry-run is visible while the modal is open.

fix.oldText:
{!preview &&

Checking…

}
fix.newText:
{!preview && purge.error &&

{purge.error.message}

} {!preview && !purge.error &&

Checking…

}

findings.title: `date` filter values go straight into the JSONB audit meta
findings.description: `created_from`/`created_to` arrive as `datetime.date` objects and are copied verbatim into `meta["filters"]`; `AuditLog.meta` is JSONB, serialized with the default `json.dumps`, which raises `TypeError: Object of type date is not JSON serializable` on flush. Any CSV export that also carries a date range (e.g. `GET /v1/admin/calls?created_from=2026-10-01&format=csv`) fails with a 500 at `await db.commit()` — the same applies to the orgs export at lines 172-175. The new tests only exercise `format=csv` with `q`, so this path is uncovered.
findings.suggestion: Consider coercing the values before handing them to `record_audit` in both places, e.g. `{k: (v.isoformat() if isinstance(v, date) else v) for k, v in filters.items() if v not in (None, "")}`, or declaring the date params as `str` and parsing them after validation.

findings.title: `/facets` runs seven unbounded aggregates, two over the whole calls table
findings.description: `distinct()` groups over `Call.status` and `Call.disconnection_reason` with no time or row bound — the `limit(100)` applies after aggregation, so each dropdown load scans every row of `calls`, which grows without a cap. The seven queries are also awaited serially.
findings.suggestion: Consider bounding the call-derived facets (e.g. `Call.started_at >= now() - 30 days`, backed by an index) and/or gathering the seven queries concurrently or caching the result for a short TTL.

findings.title: `None` passed as the gate's session breaks when billing is enabled
findings.description: `ensure_can_start_call(None, slug)` only survives because `has_credit` short-circuits on `config.enabled()` being false. With `BILLING_ENABLED` set in the environment (and the org not in `BILLING_EXEMPT_ORGS`), `ledger.balance(None, org_id)` dereferences `db.execute` and raises `AttributeError`, so the un-suspend assertion at the end of the test fails for the wrong reason.
findings.suggestion: Consider opening a session from the same private `Session` factory and passing it in, e.g. `async with Session() as db: await gate.ensure_can_start_call(db, slug)`.

fix.oldText:
async def _go(Session):
            gate.get_async_session = lambda: Session()
            await gate.ensure_can_start_call(None, slug)
fix.newText:
async def _go(Session):
            gate.get_async_session = lambda: Session()
            async with Session() as db:
                await gate.ensure_can_start_call(db, slug)

findings.title: Probe exceptions outside httpx.HTTPError escape and 500 the whole health endpoint
findings.description: `_http_ready` only catches `httpx.TimeoutException` and `httpx.HTTPError`. `httpx.InvalidURL` derives straight from `Exception`, not `HTTPError`, so a typo'd `TTS_SERVICE_URL`/`TELEPHONY_SERVICE_URL` (invalid IDNA host, stray space) propagates out of `asyncio.gather` — which runs without `return_exceptions` — and `GET /v1/admin/system` returns 500 instead of showing that one service as down. `_store_reachable` (lines 111-116) has the same catch shape.
findings.suggestion: Widen the second handler to `except Exception as exc`, the way `_timed` already does, so any probe failure degrades to a `down` row rather than failing the page.

findings.title: Re-suspending an already-suspended org silently drops the new reason
findings.description: The reason and `suspended_at` are only written when `body.suspended != controls.suspended`. A `PUT {"suspended": true, "suspended_reason": "..."}` against an org that is already suspended passes the 422 reason check, returns 200, but keeps the old reason and writes no audit entry — the caller believes the reason was updated.
findings.suggestion: Consider updating the reason whenever `body.suspended is True` (and a reason was supplied), keeping the `!=` guard only for resetting `suspended_at`.

findings.title: SIP trunk `org_slug` returns the org UUID, not a slug
findings.description: `SipTrunk.org_id` is a `UUID` FK to `organizations.id` (models.py:285-289), unlike `PhoneNumber.org_id`/`Call.org_id` which are slug strings. Serializing it under `org_slug` makes the Telephony page's "Organization" column show a raw UUID for every trunk, while the numbers table next to it shows slugs — and `TrunkRow.org_slug: string` in Telephony.tsx silently accepts it because FastAPI stringifies the UUID.
findings.suggestion: Consider joining `Organization` on `Organization.id == SipTrunk.org_id` in the trunks query and emitting `Organization.slug` here (keeping the key name), so both tables render the same identifier.

findings.title: Search fires a cross-org query per keystroke
findings.description: The query key is the path including `q`, so every character typed issues a new `/v1/admin/users` request (same in Calls.tsx:18 for `org_slug`). Each one runs the membership-count join across all tenants; typing a ten-character email means ten full scans.
findings.suggestion: Consider debouncing the input value (e.g. a ~300ms deferred value) before putting it in the query path.

findings.title: 401 from an expired access token is never handled
findings.description: The access token is minted with a 15-minute TTL (`ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_S` default 900 in services/agent/app/gateway/sessions.py:53) and the portal never calls `/v1/auth/refresh` nor reacts to a 401. After ~15 minutes of an open session every `/v1/admin/*` call throws ApiError(401); `user` stays set in AuthProvider, so Layout keeps rendering and each page just shows the error string with no way back to sign-in except manually clearing sessionStorage.
findings.suggestion: Consider treating 401 as session loss in `api()`: on `res.status === 401`, try `POST /v1/auth/refresh` (the refresh cookie is already sent via `credentials: 'include'`) and retry once, and if that fails call `setToken(null)` and drive the auth state back to the login route.

findings.title: Org search fires one cross-tenant query per keystroke
findings.description: `q` is the raw input value and sits in the query key, so every keystroke triggers a fresh `/v1/admin/orgs?q=` request, each running `name ILIKE '%…%' OR slug ILIKE '%…%'` (a leading-wildcard match that cannot use an index) plus the membership-count aggregate over all orgs. Typing a 12-character search costs 12 full scans.
findings.suggestion: Consider debouncing the value that feeds the query key (e.g. a `useDebounce`d `q` or react-query's `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` together with a ~300ms delay) so only the settled search term hits the endpoint.

findings.title: IVR pattern matches an ordinary human sentence and hangs up the call
findings.description: `\bto (?:speak|talk) (?:with|to) (?:a|an|the) (?:representative|operator|...)` is a phrase people say ("I'd rather talk to a representative", "Can I speak to an operator?"). On an outbound call with `ivr_hangup_enabled`, that single phrase makes `_handle_screened_line` latch and `_act_on_ivr` terminate the call on a live person — the exact outcome the module's own conservatism rule is meant to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Drop this pattern, or require it to co-occur with a real menu signal (a `press <digit>` / `say or press` match in the same utterance) before it counts as IVR. Note the parametrised case "To speak with a representative, please stay on the line." in tests/test_call_settings_extended.py would need updating with it.

findings.title: Webhook test endpoint is a tenant-controlled SSRF probe
findings.description: `test_agent_webhook` POSTs to any caller-supplied `body.url` after only `require_auth`, and returns `status_code` plus `latency_ms`. An org user can aim it at internal addresses (`http://127.0.0.1:8002/...`, `http://169.254.169.254/...`, service DNS names) and read a reliable up/down and timing oracle from inside the deployment network; withholding the response body does not close that. The scheme/netloc check only rejects non-HTTP URLs.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the host and reject loopback, link-local, and RFC1918 targets (and redirects to them) before probing — or route the probe through the same egress allowlist/proxy used for real deliveries.

findings.title: Deferred drain discards transcript segments banked while the agent talked
findings.description: `_drain_deferred` overwrites `_final_segments` instead of merging. During a deferral, an `is_final` segment that has not yet been flushed by a `speech_final` is appended to `_final_segments` (line 2469); when the agent finishes talking the drain replaces the whole list with the deferred text, so those words never reach the model. Trigger: sensitivity 0, caller keeps speaking and the agent's playout ends between an interim-final segment and its `speech_final`.
findings.suggestion: Prepend rather than replace, e.g. `_final_segments = [text, *_final_segments]`, so banked words survive the deferred flush.
